assertions.claim: During separation, long-distance relationships are even more stable — less contact, more imagined content
assertions.cn_span: 异地在分开期间反而更稳，因为见得少、想象成分高

assertions.claim: The real crunch comes after moving in together
assertions.cn_span: 真正的坎在搬到一起之后

assertions.claim: About half of LDR couples reached co-location, the other half ended while apart; of those who reunited, a third broke up within 3 months
assertions.cn_span: 追踪数据里约一半异地伴侣走到了同城这一步，另一半在分开期间就结束了；而重聚的这一半里，三分之一在 3 个月内分手

assertions.claim: Longer gaps between meetings and rosier imagining during separation predict less post-reunion stability
assertions.cn_span: 分开时见面间隔越长、想得越美，重聚后越不稳

assertions.claim: Prepare for the months after reunion: less personal space, more real knowledge of each other, more conflict and jealousy
assertions.cn_span: 要准备的是重聚后那几个月：自主空间变少、了解变多、冲突和吃醋变多

assertions.claim: That stability holds only while still apart; once co-located, LDR couples break up more easily
assertions.cn_span: 但这种稳定只在双方仍然分开时成立，一旦变成同城，异地伴侣更容易分手

assertions.claim: Sample: US student dating relationships, no marriage, older data — don't apply absolute proportions directly
assertions.cn_span: 样本是美国大学生的恋爱关系，不含婚姻，年代也较早，绝对比例别直接套
